accepted.s: With reference to assistance provided to Andhra Pradesh, the revenue deficit grant for 2014-15 was:
accepted.x: The revenue deficit grant for 2014-15 was ₹3,979 crore and formed part of the Special Assistance Measure.
accepted.tq: Use the year-wise numerical distinction between revenue-deficit assistance and other assistance.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Special Assistance Measure for Andhra Pradesh:
1. The total package announced under the measure was ₹24,350 crore.
2. ₹3,979 crore of this amount was towards the revenue deficit grant.
3. The remaining amount was intended for infrastructure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Special Assistance Measure was announced for ₹24,350 crore, including ₹3,979 crore as revenue deficit grant, with the balance meant for infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Test the total, component and balance together; the all-inclusive combination is correct.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s: From 2024-25 onward, the amounts specified for Amaravati and Polavaram were respectively:
accepted.x: The specified assistance was ₹15,000 crore for Amaravati and ₹12,157 crore for Polavaram.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the correct project-to-amount pairing.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the SASCI loans mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
o: ₹8,255 crore in 2024-25, ₹7,900 crore in 2025-26 and approximately ₹3,430 crore so far in 2026-27
₹7,900 crore in 2024-25, ₹8,255 crore in 2025-26 and approximately ₹3,430 crore so far in 2026-27
accepted.x: The figures stated are ₹7,900 crore for 2024-25, ₹8,255 crore for 2025-26 and approximately ₹3,430 crore so far in 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Match each figure to its financial year rather than relying only on magnitude.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SASCI assistance to Andhra Pradesh in 2026-27:
1. Andhra Pradesh can secure up to ₹8,226 crore.
2. ₹3,486 crore had been received by September 2026.
3. The amount received included ₹1,923 crore as untied capital funds and ₹1,297 crore as capex incentive.
4. A further ₹3,525 crore depended on reforms to be completed by 1 December 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the 2026-27 SASCI ceiling, receipts, components and reform-linked amount.
accepted.tq: Check every numerical component before selecting the comprehensive statement combination.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the reform-linked 2026-27 SASCI allocation?
accepted.x: The reform-linked amount included ₹1,450 crore for AgriStack and ₹950 crore for mining.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure reform-to-amount pair and eliminate the swapped figures.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about other promised assistance to Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: Releases to all the backward districts were completed without delay.
The seven districts comprised four Rayalaseema and three North Coastal districts.
Seven backward districts were covered by initial allocations.
₹2,500 crore was promised for the capital.
accepted.x: Initial allocations were made to the seven backward districts, but the releases stalled; they were not completed without delay.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the stated position on stalled releases.
accepted.sec: Special assistance to AP - amounts released year-wise

accepted.s: The Special Assistance Package for Andhra Pradesh was announced in:
accepted.x: The package was announced in September 2016 by Union Finance Minister Arun Jaitley in place of Special Category Status.
accepted.tq: Use the direct date-and-announcer recall pattern.
accepted.sec: Special Assistance Package announcement - date and components

accepted.s: The Special Assistance Package was also referred to as the:
accepted.x: The package was described as the Special Assistance Measure, abbreviated as SAM, or the Special Package.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely similar official-sounding names.
accepted.sec: Special Assistance Package announcement - date and components

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the components of the Special Assistance Package:
1. The special-assistance component was intended to equal the additional central share that Andhra Pradesh would have received as an SCS State.
2. Polavaram was treated as a national project under Section 90.
3. The Centre was to bear 100% of the remaining irrigation-component cost of Polavaram from 1 April 2014.
4. Industrial incentives were linked to Section 94(1).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the special-assistance and Polavaram provisions and the Section 94(1) industrial incentives.
accepted.tq: Verify the monetary equivalence, project status, effective date and statutory reference together.
accepted.sec: Special Assistance Package announcement - date and components

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the package is NOT correctly stated?
o: The package included a special development package for Rayalaseema and North Coastal districts.
Support was provided for specified capital institutions and buildings.
The Centre was to bridge the resource gap of Andhra Pradesh for 2014-15.
A ten-year tax holiday was implemented fully and without dilution through the package.
accepted.x: The promised ten-year tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed in the GST framework; it was not implemented fully and without dilution.
accepted.tq: Identify the over-absolute claim about tax incentives.
accepted.sec: Special Assistance Package announcement - date and components

accepted.s: The Special Assistance Package covered which period?
accepted.x: The package covered five years, from 2015-16 to 2019-20, corresponding to the promised SCS period.
accepted.tq: Test the exact five-year span rather than just the duration.
accepted.sec: Special Assistance Package announcement - date and components

accepted.s: Under the Externally Aided Projects route, which of the following best describes the repayment mechanism?
o: The State repays only the principal and the Centre bears no interest liability.
The State borrows from multilateral agencies, while the Centre repays loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
The Centre directly funds every project without any State borrowing.
The State gives up all borrowing and receives an unrestricted capital grant.
accepted.x: The State borrows from agencies such as the World Bank and ADB, and the Centre supports repayment of loan and interest up to the SCS-equivalent amount.
accepted.tq: Ask who borrows, who repays and whether the support is a grant or repayment mechanism.
accepted.sec: Externally Aided Projects route - how repayment support works

accepted.s: Which of the following institutions are examples of multilateral agencies from which Andhra Pradesh may borrow for externally aided projects?
o: Reserve Bank of India and SEBI
accepted.x: The route involves multilateral lenders such as the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank.
accepted.tq: Distinguish lending agencies from Indian constitutional, regulatory and advisory bodies.
accepted.sec: Externally Aided Projects route - how repayment support works

accepted.s: Why has Andhra Pradesh criticised the Externally Aided Projects route?
o: It excludes multilateral agencies from project financing.
It requires long approval cycles and heavy compliance, creating red tape and delays.
It provides automatic tax concessions to industries.
It prevents the use of all external finance.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has argued that long approval processes and extensive compliance requirements create red tape and delay project implementation.
accepted.tq: Link the administrative process to the stated consequence instead of confusing it with financing restrictions.
accepted.sec: Externally Aided Projects route - how repayment support works

accepted.s: The ₹15,000 crore assistance for Amaravati is currently raised through:
accepted.x: The Amaravati assistance is also raised through multilateral lenders. Andhra Pradesh prefers grants, whereas the Centre prefers loans and guarantees.
accepted.tq: Use the project-specific financing route as the decisive clue.
accepted.sec: Externally Aided Projects route - how repayment support works

accepted.s: With respect to the SCS-equivalent share in the package design, which statement is correct?
o: It was designed as a 40% central share only.
It was designed as a 90% grant-equivalent share routed through project repayments.
It was designed as a 10% grant and 90% loan for the State.
It had no relationship to the additional central share under SCS.
accepted.x: The fuller package design described support equivalent to the 90% central grant share under SCS, routed through repayment of externally aided project loans.
accepted.tq: Resolve the percentage trap by distinguishing the package design from an inconsistent isolated figure.
accepted.sec: Externally Aided Projects route - how repayment support works

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares CSS funding under SCS and the Special Assistance Package?
o: SCS: 90:10 grant and automatic; Package: equivalent money only through EAP repayments
SCS: equivalent money only through EAP repayments; Package: 90:10 grant and automatic
Both provide automatic 90:10 grants for all schemes
Neither provides any central assistance for CSS
accepted.x: Under SCS, CSS funding was a 90:10 grant and automatic. Under the package, the equivalent amount was available only through externally aided project repayments.
accepted.tq: Compare both sides of the table rather than checking only one arrangement.
accepted.sec: SCS vs Special Assistance Package - benefit by benefit

accepted.s: Which of the following benefits was associated with SCS but not provided in the same strength under the Special Assistance Package?
accepted.x: SCS included tax concessions for industry, whereas the package offered only the weaker Section 94(1) incentives.
accepted.tq: Focus on the benefit that changes in character rather than merely in delivery route.
accepted.sec: SCS vs Special Assistance Package - benefit by benefit

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SCS had a recognised category status with automatic yearly flows.
2. The Special Assistance Package was an executive package without statutory permanence.
3. SCS funds could be used across all schemes, whereas package funds were tied to approved external projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SCS had recognised and automatic features, while the package was executive in nature and tied to approved externally aided projects.
accepted.tq: Test legal footing and use-of-funds differences together.
accepted.sec: SCS vs Special Assistance Package - benefit by benefit

accepted.s: Which statement best captures Andhra Pradesh's central complaint about the Special Assistance Package?
o: The package provided stronger tax concessions than SCS.
The amount might be similar on paper, but unlike SCS it involved project-linked loans and lacked automatic flows and tax breaks.
SCS itself required all assistance to pass through external projects.
The package had no monetary component at all.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh argued that the apparent monetary equivalence did not compensate for the absence of automatic flows and tax benefits and the reliance on project-linked loans.
accepted.tq: Distinguish nominal monetary equivalence from the practical structure of benefits.
accepted.sec: SCS vs Special Assistance Package - benefit by benefit

accepted.s: The Centre cited which development as having already absorbed the benefits associated with Special Category Status?
o: The GST Council's abolition of all central assistance
The 13th Finance Commission's reduction of devolution to 32%
The 14th Finance Commission's removal of the general-special category distinction and increase of devolution to 42%
The 16th Finance Commission's restoration of revenue-deficit grants
accepted.x: The Centre relied on the 14th Finance Commission's removal of the distinction and increase of devolution to 42% as having absorbed SCS-related benefits.
accepted.tq: Use the institution, percentage and policy change as a combined identification test.
accepted.sec: Centre's stand - reasons for a package over SCS

accepted.s: According to the Centre's stated position, extending Special Category Status to Andhra Pradesh was opposed because:
o: The 14th Finance Commission recommended tax concessions only for Andhra Pradesh.
The Constitution prohibited all assistance to newly formed States.
Constitutional and technical constraints prevented extending SCS to a new State and could trigger similar demands from Bihar and Odisha.
Andhra Pradesh had already received permanent statutory SCS.
accepted.x: The Centre referred to constitutional and technical constraints and feared that granting SCS to Andhra Pradesh would lead to similar demands from Bihar and Odisha.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated policy rationale and the likely precedent effect.
accepted.sec: Centre's stand - reasons for a package over SCS

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. TDP left the NDA over the SCS demand.
B. The Special Assistance Package was announced.
C. TDP was part of the NDA while balancing alliance considerations with the SCS demand.
D. YSRCP made SCS a major 2019 campaign plank.
accepted.x: The relevant sequence is the 2014-18 alliance period, the September 2016 package announcement, the 2018 NDA exit and the 2019 campaign emphasis on SCS.
accepted.tq: Fix the broad period first, then place the 2016 announcement within it.
accepted.sec: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the political developments during 2018?
o: TDP left the NDA over SCS, while YSRCP described the package as a betrayal and made SCS a 2019 campaign plank.
The issue was settled through the 16th Finance Commission.
TDP joined the NDA over SCS and YSRCP rejected the demand.
Both TDP and YSRCP accepted the package as a permanent statutory arrangement.
accepted.x: In 2018, TDP left the NDA over SCS; YSRCP called the package a betrayal and subsequently used SCS as a major 2019 campaign issue.
accepted.tq: Pair the party action with the opposing party's political response.
accepted.sec: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time

accepted.s: During 2024-26, the Andhra Pradesh Government sought which combination of project-related assistance while again being an NDA ally?
o: Bihar's backward-area package and Odisha's capital grant
Only tax holidays and no project assistance
Only revenue-deficit grants under the 14th Finance Commission
accepted.x: During 2024-26, Andhra Pradesh sought project money for Amaravati, Polavaram and SASCI while again being an NDA ally.
accepted.tq: Use the three-project combination to distinguish the current demand from the earlier SCS campaign.
accepted.sec: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time

accepted.s: The memorandum submitted by Andhra Pradesh to the 16th Finance Commission sought:
o: Abolition of SASCI and Polavaram assistance
Lower devolution and removal of capital considerations
Only a ten-year tax holiday under Section 94(1)
accepted.x: The memorandum sought higher devolution and special weightage for the capital city.
accepted.tq: Identify the two distinct fiscal demands in the memorandum.
accepted.sec: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the figures cited by Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav in August 2026?
o: AP lost ₹3,979 crore after the 16th Finance Commission; the projected deficit was ₹16,000 crore.
AP lost ₹16,000 crore after the 14th Finance Commission; the projected deficit was ₹38,000 crore for 2025-26.
AP lost ₹48,000 crore after the 16th Finance Commission; the 2014-19 deficit was ₹38,000 crore.
AP lost up to ₹38,000 crore after the 16th Finance Commission dropped revenue-deficit grants; the revenue deficit was ₹16,000 crore during 2014-19 and projected at ₹48,000 crore for 2025-26.
accepted.x: The figures cited were a possible loss of up to ₹38,000 crore, a ₹16,000 crore revenue deficit during 2014-19 and a projected ₹48,000 crore deficit for 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Keep the three similar figures attached to their correct period and context.
accepted.sec: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the present opposition position described in relation to Special Category Status?
o: YSRCP and Congress continue to demand SCS.
Only Congress supports SCS, while YSRCP has withdrawn its demand.
Both YSRCP and Congress have accepted the package as a permanent substitute.
Neither YSRCP nor Congress has raised the SCS issue after 2018.
accepted.x: The opposition parties YSRCP and Congress continue to demand Special Category Status.
accepted.tq: Test the current political position without confusing it with the ruling alliance's project-based demands.
accepted.sec: AP Government's stand - response and demands over time
